title: Compose actual CRT/Tensor sandwich with conditional two-S recovery
body:
## Result and scope

Connect the actual PR4024 encoded CRT converter to the PR3935 physical Tensor for the complete three-transform convolution schedule, four exact real word products per coordinate, opposite transform, both S scales, nearest integer recovery, inverse CRT and carry return. The new written proof gives an encoded strict precision guard and retains every inherited analytic, geometry, native and setup-cost premise.

This is a conditional caller and finite conformance package, not a production multiplier, new Gaussian identity, selected supplier or improved bound. The actual coprime (5,7) to (8,8), p48/P80 reduced-page fixture executes all three Tensor and three Converter calls and matches an independent staged oracle. Its diagnostic output is 0 while the true product is 345550037539; default production entry rejects the reduced catalogue. A separate p96 recovery leaf checks supplied dyadic approximations, both S factors and carry arithmetic with exact margin controls. Raising p alone does not fix this fixture's production geometry.

The entry ABI rejects all metadata/data aliases and all descendant private tapes before Count reads. Constructor ownership checks cover fixed resident topology, closed owners, empty pools and dirty/shared child controls. A pending-return token prevents the occupied-output end-head bypass, and explicit consume performs the paid clear/marker retirement.

## Sources and evidence

- PR3935: Jose Manuel / jmbarrancoml, final head f687fa171ef760fa98a4be1289717b47dd4ee0b3.
- PR4024: Tekalign / tekuuu, e99297be6749518a1b5b85cd129ecaf204d26c63. The shared lifecycle token only unifies the authenticated Tape cohort; source/interface compatibility is separately documented.
- PR2313: Mason Hale's prior dense rigorous recovery is credited and not duplicated.
- Frozen source07/source08 retain the Fourier/CRT/convolution identities. Source bodies, archives, notices and selected frontier are unchanged.

Python 3.12 normal and optimized light checks pass, including six metadata aliases, five private descendant aliases, dirty/shared/nonclosed constructor controls, end-head output consumption and next valid entry, p88 rejection/p89 scalar acceptance, exact p96 enclosure, missing-one-S and CRT-versus-identity discriminators (not a standalone wrong-Fourier-R mutant). Source history, committed bytes and official 83-file export integrity pass. Final Git-free optimized full replay passed in 372.34 seconds at e65f47db55b9a3779fbf7fe23e93a8a4c5eb3ce1; every exported file remained unchanged. Final source-drift rejection and exact restoration also passed. Official export SHA256: fd6dfe01167dbe9b93826f614ed6fb4e1574c3139fe774ec9c3447ed8012f771. The original 375.56-second full run is retained as pre-hardening evidence only.

Open next questions: bind production-generated pages and native realization to all analytic/geometry premises; then bind arbitrary n-bit packing to an admitted all-size parameter family with full preparation costs. These are required before complete multiplication or supplier admission claims.

Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3664#discussioncomment-19141165

Submission refresh: canonical main81e9bd69e4a5b00ba9c713a1620e36d576d5522e leaves governing guidance, selected record and declared inputs unchanged. Complete refreshed overlap snapshot at08:48–08:49UTC covered312 open PRs,4214 Discussion records and6824 local HEAD notes; unpublished work remains outside coverage.

Hosted verification limitation: the Ubuntu 24.04.5 / CPython 3.12.15 job passed the leaves in 5.40 seconds, but the complete optimized full invocation timed out at the unchanged 600-second cap. The final local Git-free full replay passed in 372.34 seconds on macOS arm64 / CPython 3.12.2; it does not establish hosted portability. Follow-up commit `467445ad6` documents this unresolved limitation and a future equivalent-optimization obligation. All scientific code, receipts, inputs, frozen dependencies and registered checks are byte-identical to `e65f47db`; no full replay was repeated for the documentation-only change.
